title: DeAR: Decentralized Agentic Reasoning via Capability Grounding and Collaborative Thought Navigation
abstract: arXiv:2608.17282v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Existing agentic reasoning systems typically rely on centralized protocols. This design introduces routing bottlenecks and static role allocations that often fail when handling complex multimodal queries. We propose DeAR (Decentralized Agentic Reasoning), a framework that shifts from central control to autonomous peer-to-peer collaboration. DeAR is built on three mechanisms: (1) decentralized capability grounding for query-dependent agent specialization, (2) thought map navigation for targeted peer interactions, and (3) topology update for adaptive error correction. Evaluations across 9 diverse multimodal reasoning and text-based QA benchmarks indicate that DeAR consistently outperforms recent baseline methods, validating that decentralized and adaptive collaboration among agents enhances accuracy in knowledge-intensive reasoning tasks. The source code will be available at https://open_upon_acceptance.

translated_title: DeAR：通过能力锚定与协作思维导航实现去中心化智能体推理
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17282v1 公告类型：新论文  摘要：现有的智能体推理系统通常依赖集中式协议。这种设计在处理复杂的多模态查询时，往往会导致路由瓶颈和静态角色分配问题，从而失效。我们提出了DeAR（去中心化智能体推理），一个将控制从中心转向自主点对点协作的框架。DeAR基于三个机制构建：（1）去中心化能力锚定，用于根据查询实现智能体专业化；（2）思维地图导航，用于针对性的同伴交互；（3）拓扑更新，用于自适应错误修正。在9个多样化的多模态推理和基于文本的问答基准测试中，DeAR持续优于最近的基线方法，验证了去中心化和自适应智能体协作能提高知识密集型推理任务的准确性。源代码将在https://open_upon_acceptance 提供。
tldr: DeAR通过去中心化的能力锚定、思维地图导航和拓扑更新机制，实现了智能体间的自主点对点协作，在多种推理基准上显著提升了准确性。
en_tdlr: DeAR enables autonomous peer-to-peer collaboration among agents through decentralized capability grounding, thought map navigation, and topology updates, significantly improving accuracy across diverse reasoning benchmarks.
